title: (Michif) Michif Country
description: (Michif, French) Michif Country welcomes Plains Cree rapper Drezus, who has been drafted onto the crew to assist with pulling up dozens of fishing nets and processing the big haul. Fishing season is winding down, and the mad dash has begun to finish.

title: (Michif) Red River Gold
description: (Michif, French) In the Caribou Bog, the team searches for two cannons lost by Wolseley's military expedition. And the team comes across the most treacherous ground so far.

title: (Nsyilxcen) Quest Out West Wild Food
description: (Nsyilxcen) Tracey meets author Elaine Alec who discusses her book and her efforts in the Indigenous community. Tracey goes on to meet Denise Lecoy and her granddaughter to make a traditional rattle. She then completes her journey with her friend.

title: (Nsyilxcen) Quest Out West Wild Food
description: (Nsyilxcen) Tracey discusses day schools and the impact they have had. She meets Toni George, the principal at Outma Sqilx'w Cultural School, and is serenaded by the school's students. Afterwards, Tracey and Toni prepare a delicious meal together.

title: (Nsyilxcen) Merchants of the Wild
description: (Nsyilxcen) As their journey comes to an end, fast waters and quick-changing weather threaten to break the group's spirits. On the edge of emotional turmoil, a visit from an Elder brings a surprise that no one expected.

title: (Mi'kmaq) Teepee Time
description: (Mi'kmaq) Spend time with Teepee as he puts away the groceries and helps prepare supper for the very first time.

title: (Wolastoqey) Lil Glooscap and the Legends of Turtle Island
description: (Wolastoqey) Lil Glooscap and friends learn that when we do something sooner rather than later, we can help solve or prevent a problem before it happens. Our actions in the present can sometimes make things easier for us in the future!

title: (Inuktitut) Tuktu
description: (Inuktitut, South Baffin) Tiri plans to go sledding with his friends, but right as he is leaving his mom asks him to watch his siblings. Tiri is disappointed but wants to help his family. His friends offer to help babysit, and they all go sledding.

title: (Inuktitut) Anaana's Tent
description: (Inuktitut, North and South Baffin) Rita Claire loves to go hunting and, in the summer, she hunts whales, seals, caribou, fish and birds. Kathleen Merritt visits the qarmaq and sings Imutaa. Looee Arreak teaches how to sew a sealskin for framing.

title: (Cree) Tiga Talk
description: (Cree) Jodie and Jason get to watch as different kinds of buildings are being built. They visit construction sites, a teepee and then do a little building of their own. Tiga is very happy with the results!

title: (Anishinaabemowin) Chums
description: (Anishinaabemowin, Central) A peaceful fishing day for Emiree and Ira turns chaotic with pelicans dominating the lake. The Chums work collaboratively to negotiate a shared space, ensuring all can enjoy the lake harmoniously.

title: (Halkomelem) Coyote's Crazy Smart Science Show
description: (Halkomelem) Find out why salmon are important to so many Indigenous nations as our Science Questers visit a salmon hatchery.

title: (Kanienʼkéha) Dreamcatchers
description: (Kanienʼkéha) When the Dreamcatchers catch a dream about toxic waste flooding a Reserve, they must find the Dreamer, unlock her ancestral superpowers and stop the dream from coming true!

title: (Inuktitut) Warrior Up!
description: (Inuktitut, South Baffin) Five young Cherokee women train to retrace the infamous Trail of Tears their ancestors endured during their forced displacement 200 years ago. The women ready themselves emotionally and physically for a gruelling bike ride.

title: (Inuktitut) Ajungi!
description: (Inuktitut, South Baffin) Elisha Kilabuk teaches Eli Lawson how to skin a ptarmigan, a small land bird traditionally eaten by Inuit.

title: (Kanienʼkéha) Princesses
description: (Kanienʼkéha) Indigenous fashion extends way beyond runways; it's not just about how it looks, it's about how it is made. The process of creating Indigenous clothing, jewelry and footwear is even more important than what the articles represent.

title: (Kanienʼkéha) Working It out Together
description: (Kanienʼkéha) Alexa has her first workout with Derek, and it proves to be too much for her to handle. We meet Sophie-Claude who is reeling from the recent passing of her parents. The Fab Four learn self-defense.

title: (Kanienʼkéha) One Dish, One Spoon
description: (Kanienʼkéha) Tawnya visits Tyendinaga with her sons to reconnect with land and family. Cousin Eli teaches the boys to trap fishers, while Tawnya explores a bison farm and cooks a bush dinner of bison hand pies and maple-candied fruit.

title: (Cree) Indians and Aliens
description: (Cree) Ernest Webb meets with Mary Jane and Gilbert Cazon, two Dene knowledge keepers in the Northwest Territories. They've spent the last 40 years cataloguing their many strange encounters with UFOs, including the time they were chased by a UFO.

title: (Cree) Pow Wow Chow
description: (Cree, Swampy) Nostalgia fills the final day at Curve Lake as Shawn gets reinforcements from past mentors, Rhonda recounts Bob's management style and Art and Amy tell a Wikwemikong love story.

title: (Michif) Métis Foodies
description: (Michif, Heritage) Suzanne and Paulette prep for their Christmas Cocktail Party, making festive treats with family. The episode ends in a huge gathering filled with music, laughter and plenty of punch!

title: (Michif) Chaos and Courage
description: (Michif) Driven underground for over a century, midwifery is enjoying a long-overdue reclamation. Meet the Indigenous women at the helm of this movement, and discover how this ancient practice benefits mothers, children and entire communities.

title: (Salish) Warrior Games
description: (Salish) Host Steve Sxwithul'txw tries his hand at archery, a skill being revitalized by dozens of First Nations and Métis clubs. For its original practitioners, it was far more than just a sport.

title: (Nisga'a) Ocean Warriors: Mission Ready
description: (Nisga'a) As the Quatsino Nation Coast Guard Auxiliary battles shifting tides and looming storms to search for a missing mushroom picker, the legend of Bak'was, Quatsino's wild man of the woods, resurfaces.

title: (Mi'kmaq) Gespe'gewa'gi: The Last Land
description: (Mi'kmaq) Albert and his son Chris go on a fishing trip together. All is calm until the boat's hydraulics start acting up. The pair need to rely on each other and use some creative problem-solving to keep their trip afloat.

title: APTN National News Weekend
description: Bringing the week full circle with a recap of the top national news stories of the week.

description: (Inuktitut, South Baffin) After finishing a family camping trip, Taqu helps her mom pack up the tent. Uka gets stressed when he receives a bad grade on a test he thought he'd aced, but Tiu-Tiu helps him calm down.

title: (Inuktitut) Ukaliq and Kalla
description: (Inuktitut, South Baffin) Ukaliq and Kalla enjoy a weekend at their tent, making tea and bannock after Kalla picks heather. Later, Ukaliq returns from boating with a baby seagull, and Kalla teaches him that caring for a pet is a big responsibility.

description: (Cree) Come sing and dance with Bizou as she takes you on a picturesque journey into the wonderful world of salmon, Canada's great migratory fish.

title: (Cree) Coyote's Crazy Smart Science Show
description: (Cree) In this episode, Sto:lo knowledge keeper Dr. Gwen Point tells the story of the man who became a cedar tree and teaches the Science Questers about cedar technology. Peter Gong shows them how he makes bentwood boxes using new tools.

title: (Kanienʼkéha) Dreamcatchers
description: (Kanienʼkéha) And a one and a two and a three... Determined to stop it from jeopardizing the environment, the Dreamcatchers tackle a gas-guzzling race-car derby. Can they keep the Earth safe from this high-speed menace?

title: (Inuktitut) Uakallanga
description: (Inuktitut, South Baffin) Teena Kakee learns about seal skins with John Eetuk. Inuit use seal skins for their shelter, clothing, tools and more. Preparing the seal skins is a laborious rite of passage for women, taking weeks or months to complete.

title: (Inuktitut) Nunavummi Mamarijavut
description: (Inuktitut, South Baffin) In this episode of Nunavummi Mamarijavut, we watch a beluga whale being harvested. Then our host Zipporah Ungalaq learns how to make a unique pizza from the beluga meat or maqtaaq.

title: (Innu-aimun) Chuck and the First Peoples' Kitchen
description: (Innu-aimun, Uashat and Pessamit) In Kangiqsujuaq, Chuck joins Noah Annahatak, one of Nunavik's top hunters. They go by boat to a great location and shoot a caribou near the shore. They field dress the animal on site and return to the village.

title: (Innu-aimun) De Pessamit à Sheshatshiu
description: (Innu-aimun, Uashat and Pessamit) Instrument banni par les missionnaires européens dès leur arrivée, le tambour a persisté à travers les siècles. Aujourd'hui, devant l'orchestre symphonique de Montréal, l'aîné Api Bellefleur le met à l'honneur en.

title: (Cree) Red Earth Uncovered
description: (Cree, Plains) Shayla takes a tour of Cadboro Bay in search of Caddy.

title: (Cree) Wild Rose Vets
description: (Cree, Plains) Dr. Allison and her team must monitor Shelby the Shih Tzu while trying to remove hundreds of tiny, grainy bladder stones. In Calgary, Dr. Emma and her team are trying to wrangle dogs for a blood drive, emphasis on trying!

title: (Michif) Amplify
description: (Michif, French) Haida band Jason Camp and The Posers reveal how their beautiful home of Haida Gwaii inspires their unique brand of punk music. The band's two frontmen and their manager create music that celebrates the strength and rich culture.

title: (Michif) Nation Untamed
description: (Michif, Heritage) Sam and Chuck journey to Canada's Arctic, gaining a new appreciation for the far North and the people who live there. They experience a landscape and a traditional hunt unlike any they have witnessed before.

title: (Salish) Warrior Games
description: (Salish) Host Steve Sxwithul'txw tries his hand at archery, a skill being revitalized by dozens of First Nations and Métis clubs. For its original practitioners, it was far more than just a sport.

title: (Halkomelem) Nations at War
description: (Halkomelem) In 1676, the Mohawks made an alliance with Great Britain, ensuring assistance through war and hardship. One hundred years later, this promise forced the Mohawks to choose between a new nation and their old allies.

title: (Wolastoqey) Petroglyphs to Pixels
description: (Wolastoqey) This episode celebrates Haida artists as they pay tribute to cedar, a keystone species essential to Haida Gwaii's ecosystem and a fundamental element in Haida art.

title: (Mi'kmaq) Spirit Talker
description: (Mi'kmaq) Shawn makes a strong spirit connection at the site of a former residential school near Sipekne'katik First Nation. A young mother hears from her only son who passed away unexpectedly; a brother's spirit guides his sister.

title: (Mi'kmaq) Spirit Talker
description: (Mi'kmaq)In the heart of the Cowichan Tribes,Shawn delves into the rich culinary tradition of preparing smoking sockeye salmon with chef Jared Williams.Amidst the spirit sessions,a profound connection unfolds a man reunites with his departed mother.
